title: HTTP/1.1 server in Java
tagline: A single-thread, non-blocking web server built on java.nio, with no frameworks.
summary: A web server written from scratch in Java with java.nio and no frameworks. One thread handles every connection through non-blocking I/O. It listens on several ports, supports GET, POST and DELETE, chunked requests, file uploads, cookies and sessions, runs CGI scripts, and takes all its behavior from a configuration file. challenges.title: Many clients, one thread
challenges.problem: One thread per client wastes memory, and a single blocking read would freeze the whole server.
challenges.solution: Non-blocking channels registered on a `java.nio` Selector. The event loop only reads or writes a socket when it is ready, so one thread can serve every client.

challenges.title: Requests that arrive in pieces
challenges.problem: With non-blocking I/O, one request can arrive over several reads, and a chunked body does not announce its total size.
challenges.solution: Each connection keeps its own buffer and parsing state, and the parser only moves to the next step (headers, body, next chunk) once enough bytes have arrived. [TODO: confirm this matches your implementation]

challenges.title: Running CGI scripts
challenges.problem: A CGI script is an external program. The server must pass it the request and read its output without stopping the other clients.
challenges.solution: Scripts run in their own process started with `ProcessBuilder`, with request data passed through environment variables and standard input, as the CGI standard defines. [TODO: explain how you kept the event loop from blocking while the script runs]
